analysis.title: Weekend Prep (Brian Garrett) - 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: Index-level volatility looks calm while single-stock and credit markets price stress. 2027 is priced as one of the least correlated 12-month periods in the dataset, with SPX 12m implied correlation (ATMF) near 20%, one of the lowest levels in history.

SPX and NDX rose three straight sessions Mon-Wed (SPX +150bps, NDX +300bps) as participants adopted an 8th-inning framework. NDX then fell 140bps Thursday and 350bps Friday, forcing portfolio re-underwriting.
Garrett lists contra-indicators suggesting the lower spot level may be healing: macro equity vol is starting to price nervousness, which index vol had refused to do before.
Net exposure is rising as a result of risk-off flow. Equities were net bought overall, but largely through short covering.
Stocks are no longer 'crashing up'. For some of the largest companies, 2026 volatility came from the right tail, and that is no longer the case.
Index valuations are catching down to earnings. SPX is +10.7% YTD while forward P/E is about 19x, the lowest level of 2026.

Factor extremes: the dividend yield factor is in the 90th percentile and the valuation factor in the 80th percentile (10y), so safe is expensive. Momentum is in the 30th percentile and growth in the 40th, so they are cheap.
Credit experts suggest AI financing needs could surprise to the downside. A lower requirement from the bond market would reduce anxiety but takes time to play out.
Retail buy-the-dip behavior is showing hesitation, with the cohort now asking before buying dips. Garrett sees retail on the verge of change with agentic tools.
Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in four weeks, but largely through short covering in macro.
TMT was the most bought sector on the week but is still heavily sold month to date for October. Mag7 length remains near YTD highs.
The decrease in prime brokerage net exposure has been well flagged. GS regressed it against SPX drawdowns and finds these net levels have been associated with drawdowns greater than 20%.
The GS desk sold net $4.2B of tech delta on Friday and finished the week as a net seller, reversing a mid-week buy skew, with about a $10B peak-to-trough skew on the week.

CTA flows: SPX closed 35 handles above the medium-term threshold and NDX closed below both the short and medium-term thresholds. Garrett expects a red sweep across equity systematics pending Monday's update.
Gamma has not repriced to the extent of vol and skew. 0DTE straddles stayed consistently priced despite large realized moves, and there is no excess variance priced for the midterms.
US equity options traded almost 100 million contracts Friday, the fourth highest volume session on record.
Downside volatility is now more extreme than upside volatility, and skew has already repriced for this in the short run.
Year-end straddles with 42 sessions left in 2026: SPX +/-5.1%, NDX +/-7.8%, RTY +/-6.3%. Large cap vol exceeds small cap vol again.
The basket team has pair trades for midterm themes: health insurance affordability, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending, and corporate tax beneficiaries.

The Wednesday SPX straddle captures AAPL earnings and the midterms, yet it costs 30bps less than Friday's single-session move (150bps implied vs -180bps realized Friday).

tension_points.bull_case: Spot weakness may be healing: macro equity vol is starting to price nervousness, valuations are catching down to earnings (forward P/E about 19x, the 2026 low), and stocks are no longer crashing up.
tension_points.bear_case: PB net levels are associated with drawdowns above 20% in GS's regression, AI length is still being unwound, and CTAs are expected to show a red sweep across equity systematics.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A red sweep across equity systematics in Monday's CTA update would support the bear case.
